clue.text: Sweet turning up a little more acidic

indicators.note: turning up says the hidden letters are read backwards
a little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sweet that tastes a bit sharper, turning upward in someone's mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turning up' reads the run OREA, found in 'mORE Acidic', from bottom to top. Aero is a British chocolate bar full of bubbles.
explanation.definitionFit: Aero is a brand of aerated chocolate bar sold in Britain, so it is a sweet.

clue.text: Facial feature fed nougat initially, same part spitting out old humbug

indicators.note: the facial feature is fed, so a letter goes inside it

parts.note: the nose is a feature of the face

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of nougat

parts.note: first letter of nougat

indicators.note: spitting out means a letter is expelled from that part

parts.note: the same part as before, the facial feature again

explanation.surface: Someone's mouth crammed with nougat spits the old humbug out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humbug' looks like another sweet in this sweet-themed puzzle, but here it means rubbish talk. NOSE takes N to make NONSE; NOSE again, without O, gives NSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Humbug as an exclamation or noun means deceptive talk or rubbish, a synonym for foolish talk.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a knitted top or sweater
second meaning: a breed of cattle, so beef in a loose, question-marked sense

explanation.walkthrough: 'Top beef' suggests the best cut of meat; the two words instead give a garment and a breed of cow, named after the Channel Island.
explanation.definitionFit: A jersey is a pullover garment, and Jersey cattle are a breed originating on that island.

parts.note: Polo is a British brand of mint sweet with a hole
to neck is to kiss and cuddle

explanation.surface: A sweet kiss suggests things are getting warmer between two people.
explanation.walkthrough: A Polo is a ring-shaped British mint; to neck is old-fashioned slang for to kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-collared sweater keeps the throat snug, so it is a garment that heats the wearer, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Player is inspired by emotionless type, but no leader

indicators.note: inspired by means breathed into, so a piece goes inside another
no leader means the first letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a robot is a person who shows no feeling

explanation.surface: A musician draws inspiration from a cold, unfeeling figure who leads nobody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' could be a sportsman or actor; the robot's music connection is the woodwind instrument, and 'no leader' strips the robot's first letter before IS goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboist plays the oboe, so is a musical performer in an orchestra.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an exclamation of surprise
second meaning: a shaft sunk to reach underground water

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like someone pointing out a spring; it is two separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an interjection of surprise and a hole dug to draw groundwater.

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the sack is slang for bed
love is zero in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: Pillow talk: sweet nothings whispered in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet nothing' looks like one phrase but splits: 'Sweet' is the definition, as a term of endearment.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet and beloved are both affectionate terms for a dearly loved person.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a shoemaker, who works with a last, the foot-shaped mould
second meaning: a baked fruit dessert with a scone topping

explanation.walkthrough: 'Last worker' suggests the final person on shift; a last is a shoemaker's foot form.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobbler mends shoes on a last, and a cobbler is also a fruit pudding, sweet being British for dessert.

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a deer putting on a show; the word is both a plural noun and a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Female deer are called does, and 'does' is the present tense of 'to do', meaning carries out.

indicators.note: something incomprehensible is jumbled, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A piece of writing so confusing it only makes sense in places.
explanation.definitionFit: Sectorial means relating to or divided into sectors, that is, split into sections.

clue.text: Sweet line in fresh torte after drink

indicators.note: after puts the rest following the drink

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

indicators.note: in places the line within the rearranged cake
fresh means the letters of torte are made anew, rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe: a fresh torte with a line of cream, served after a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Cha is British slang for tea, from Chinese.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlotte is a dessert of fruit or custard set inside a casing of bread or sponge fingers.

clue.text: Every other part of icky sweet

indicators.note: every other part means alternate letters of the word are picked, the second and fourth

parts.note: a four-letter word whose even-placed letters are the two that matter

explanation.surface: Describing something sickly sweet, every bit of it icky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Every other part of' picks the second and fourth letters of 'icky', C and Y; say 'C and Y' as one word to get the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Candy is the American word for confectionery, sweets in British use.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Colón, a port city at the Caribbean end of the Panama Canal
second meaning: the punctuation mark itself

explanation.walkthrough: The colon at the end looks like ordinary punctuation, but it is the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Colón is a Panamanian port city, and the two-dot punctuation mark is called a colon.

parts.note: pert means bright and lively
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: A gap appearing in a fast-flowing river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a Yorkshire river, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperture is an opening or hole, the same as a gap.

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: An art critic asking whether a painting is rubbish or a Turner.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner looks like the painter J M W Turner; the question mark warns it means something that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the rotating part of a machine such as a helicopter, so it spins.

explanation.walkthrough: 'Down and dirty' reads as a stock phrase; it is two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue describes a gloomy mood and also risqué jokes or films.

clue.text: Kiwi's heading beyond valley — it can't take flight!

indicators.note: beyond means the next piece comes after the valley

parts.note: a dale is a valley

indicators.note: heading takes the opening letter of the word

parts.note: first letter of Kiwi's

explanation.surface: A kiwi heading over a valley, though the bird cannot fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests the flightless kiwi, but means a flight of stairs: Daleks, the Doctor Who villains, were famously unable to climb them.
explanation.definitionFit: Daleks are the wheeled robotic aliens of Doctor Who, mocked for being stopped by staircases.

clue.text: Red Sea rising over a source of sweetness

indicators.note: over in a down clue means placed above the next piece
rising in a down clue means the letters read upwards

parts.note: rare meat is red inside
the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: The Red Sea rising above something sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red Sea' looks like the one body of water but splits in two: red as in rare steak, and the Med, short for the Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: Demerara is a brown cane sugar, so a sweetener.

clue.text: Sweet stick gathering last of sherbet

indicators.note: gathering means the stick takes a letter in

parts.note: a cue is the stick used in snooker or billiards

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of the word

parts.note: last letter of sherbet

explanation.surface: A lolly stick picking up the last of the sherbet.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute and sweet both describe something charming and endearing.

parts.note: cut means cancelled, dropped
an ad is a commercial
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A television show cancelled, with only the commercial surviving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Showboat' looks like a noun for a riverboat theatre; it is a verb meaning to show off.
explanation.definitionFit: To showboat is to show off, and to cut a dash is to make a stylish impression.

clue.text: Temporarily stop during school period, computer studies

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'
a term is a period of the school year
IT, information technology, is the school subject of computing

explanation.surface: A pupil halting schoolwork part way through a term of computing lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: To intermit is to suspend or pause for a time.

indicators.note: in puts the cube inside the dessert

parts.note: afters is British slang for dessert, the sweet course
eight is a cube number, two times two times two

explanation.surface: A sugar cube dropped into a sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'sugar cube' would be the natural reading; it is the number 8. After Eights are thin British chocolate mints.
explanation.definitionFit: After Eights are a brand of chocolate-covered mint wafers, a kind of confectionery.

clue.text: Cosmic rays primarily penetrating new atlas

indicators.note: penetrating means one piece goes into the other
new means the letters of atlas are made into a fresh arrangement
primarily takes the opening letter of the word

parts.note: first letter of rays

explanation.surface: Cosmic rays passing through a brand-new atlas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cosmic rays' looks like one phrase; 'Cosmic' alone is the definition. ATLAS rearranged becomes ASTAL, with R inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Astral means relating to the stars, hence of outer space.

clue.text: As beer gut wobbles, something sweet in that

indicators.note: a wobbling belly shakes about, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A drinker's paunch wobbling, with something sugary inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar beet is a root crop grown for the sucrose it contains, refined into table sugar.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: one of the four ... in cards

explanation.walkthrough: 'Executive clubs' suggests private business clubs; the words split into two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A suit is slang for a corporate manager, and clubs is one of the card suits.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for a detective
second meaning: spotted ... is a British suet pudding with currants

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' seems to mean seen by the sleuth; it is the first word of the pudding's name, its spots being currants.
explanation.definitionFit: Dick is old slang for a private investigator, and spotted dick is a traditional British dessert.

clue.text: Part of leg in small 3, say

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the fleshy back of the lower leg
second meaning: a young Jersey, the cow breed from 3 down

explanation.walkthrough: '3' points to the answer of 3 down, read as the cattle breed; a small one is a young cow.
explanation.definitionFit: The calf is the muscle at the back of the shin, and a calf is a young bovine.

clue.text: Fudge is wrong after starter of dumplings

indicators.note: after means the rest follows that letter
starter of takes the opening letter of the word

parts.note: first letter of dumplings
a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: Fudge served wrongly after a starter of dumplings.
explanation.walkthrough: In this sweet-themed puzzle 'Fudge' looks like the confection; it is the verb meaning to falsify.
explanation.definitionFit: To fudge figures is to misrepresent or twist them.

clue.text: Sweet, in the style of sweet wine

parts.note: Mars is a British chocolate bar
à la means in the style of

explanation.surface: A sweet made in the manner of a dessert wine.
explanation.walkthrough: A Mars bar is a chocolate bar; à la is French for in the manner of.
explanation.definitionFit: Marsala is a fortified Sicilian wine, often sweet and used in desserts.
